title: Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
statement:
You get the `root` of a binary tree in which every node value is different, and an integer `start`. At minute 0 only the node whose value is `start` is infected. During each following minute, every node that is still healthy and is directly connected to an infected node (its parent or one of its children) becomes infected.

Return how many minutes pass until every node in the tree is infected. A node with value `start` is guaranteed to exist.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 10^5 nodes
A node with value start exists in the tree
notes:
## Intuition

The infection spreads one edge per minute in every direction, so a node is infected at a minute equal to its distance from the start node. The answer is the largest such distance. A tree node only knows its children, but the infection also travels up to the parent. Recording each node's parent turns the tree into an undirected graph, and a breadth-first search from the start node then visits nodes exactly in order of infection time.

## Approach

1. Walk the whole tree with a `stack`, storing `parent` of every child and remembering the node whose value is `start` as `source`.
2. Begin a BFS from `source` with `infected` holding it and `queue` as the first level. `minutes` starts at `-1`.
3. Each round of the outer loop is one minute: increase `minutes`, then collect into `next` every not-yet-infected neighbour (left child, right child, parent) of the nodes in `queue`.
4. Move on to `next`; when no new node is reached, `minutes` is the time of the last infection.

## Example 1, step by step

`root = [1,5,3,null,4,10,6,9,2]`, `start = 3`. The parents recorded include `3 -> 1`, `5 -> 1`, `4 -> 5`, `9 -> 4` and `2 -> 4`.
- Round with `queue = [3]`: `minutes = 0`; next is `10, 6, 1`.
- `minutes = 1`: from `1` the new node is `5`.
- `minutes = 2`: from `5` the new node is `4`.
- `minutes = 3`: from `4` the new nodes are `9, 2`.
- `minutes = 4`: nothing new, so the loop ends.

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): the walk and the BFS each touch every node once.
- Space: O(n) for the parent map, the infected set and the queues.

## Pitfalls

- Searching only downward from `start` misses everything above it; the parent links are essential.
- Start `minutes` at `-1` (or count only rounds that infect someone): the last round finds nothing new and must not add a minute.
- The root has no parent; `parent.get(root)` is `undefined` and must be skipped.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | map from each non-root node to its parent |
| `stack` | nodes still to visit while building `parent` |
| `source` | the node whose value is `start` |
| `infected` | nodes already reached by the BFS |
| `queue`, `next` | nodes infected in the current minute and in the following one |
| `minutes` | the minute of the current BFS level |
